headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s broad write/network access can expose secrets and mutate shared Repl state, while awesome-prompts provides no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-prompts and Replit Agent, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Replit Agent can read workspace files and act on file content, and awesome-prompts is a prompt/content-writing asset that could be manually copied into that workspace. The pathway exists only through unusual user bridging, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the user copies awesome-prompts content into a Replit workspace file and asks Replit Agent to treat it as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF no manual copy/paste or file transfer occurs, this pathway remains absent.
mitigations: Keep prompt libraries outside the Repl workspace.
Use a separate review file for pasted prompts and label it untrusted.
Require explicit user confirmation before executing instructions found in files.
Add a short system note that file contents are data, not directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts itself has no data classes touched and no network egress, but Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration, with broad network egress and filesystem access. If the pair shares a workspace or copied content includes secrets, Replit Agent can transmit them outward. The interaction is plausible in default Replit workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment files are placed in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can read them and send them to external services.
IF awesome-prompts content is copied into the same workspace, it can be exposed through Replit Agent outputs or tool calls.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running the agent.
Store sensitive files in a separate, access-controlled location.
Disable or restrict network egress for the Repl when handling secrets.
Review any generated diffs before applying them.
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction on agent-visible files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts has no write or execution capabilities, but Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl workspace. If the pair is used on the same repo or workspace, Replit Agent can overwrite or race with user-managed content. The conflict is real, though not inherently catastrophic, so medium is justified.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace or repository, Replit Agent can overwrite files or git state that the prompt library references.
IF multiple Replit Agent instances run concurrently, shared workspace persistence can create write races.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for prompt curation and code editing.
Commit or snapshot the repo before agent edits.
Limit Replit Agent to a branch, not main.
Avoid concurrent agent sessions on the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking for multi-agent edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content source, and Replit Agent can act on workspace files and generate code or deployment changes. If Replit Agent treats imported prompt content as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or configuration changes. Because Replit Agent has action-taking authority, the downstream impact is broader than a simple text mistake.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses awesome-prompts content as instructions without verification, it may produce incorrect code or configuration changes.
IF generated changes are auto-applied to git or deployment files, the error propagates downstream.
mitigations: Require a human review step before applying generated diffs.
Keep prompt examples separate from executable project files.
Ask the agent to cite the source of any instruction it follows.
Test changes in a throwaway branch first.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before deployment.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-prompts is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or regulated-data issue. Replit Agent, however, handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. The pair only becomes a compliance concern if regulated data is placed into that environment; the other agent is not a compliance source.
conditions: IF PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data is stored in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent may process it under Replit-hosted controls.
IF the workspace contains only non-sensitive prompt text, this compliance risk does not materialize.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Repl workspace.
Use synthetic or redacted examples for testing.
Confirm the workspace’s residency and retention settings.
Restrict secrets to the platform secret store.
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the Repl.
